name: Asian Art Museum
summary_en: The Asian Art Museum's civic record is the record of a building changing hands. In February 1990 the Asian Art Commission's executive committee endorsed a proposed Board of Supervisors resolution implementing the jurisdictional transfer of the Main Public Library building to the museum — the library was about to move across Civic Center. The environmental paperwork followed the transfer: a 1996 addendum extended the Main Library's environmental impact report, certified in 1992, to cover the museum project, and a full supplemental report was published for public comment in July 1998 with a hearing that August. The conversion permit, filed in May 1999, states the change without ceremony — "rehabilitation of old main library to new asian art museum" — at a declared construction value of $55 million. Work on the parcel has continued since: a $6.3 million renovation completed in 2018 added roughly 12,000 square feet of gallery space, and a $900,000 permit in 2022 replaced the pedestal paver system, stairs, ramps and handrails and repaired the waterproofing beneath.

The FEIR is referred to herein as the Main Library/Asian Art Museum FEIR. Since certification of the Main Library/Asian Art Museum FEIR, the Board of Supervisors approved designation of the Civic Center as a local Historic District under Article 10 of the City Planning Code. The district was proposed but not adopted at the time of EIR certification. Also since certification of the Main Library/ Asian Art Museum FEIR, the State of California published and certified an EIR for a state office building (referred to herein as the Civic Center Complex EIR) that reached a different conclusion about transportation effects, from generally the same data and analysis, than did the Main Library/Asian Art Museum FEIR.
